💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 17:00, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 17:08.
  • Tottenham Hotspur youngster Luca Williams-Barnett repaid Roberto De Zerbi's faith in him with a goal and assist in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Ipswich Town.
  • The 18-year-old was handed his first Premier League start against the Tractor Boys in place of the injured Mathys Tel, having shown glimpses of his potential off the bench against Leeds United and Crystal Palace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 17:00, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 17:08.

Tottenham Hotspur youngster Luca Williams-Barnett repaid Roberto De Zerbi's faith in him with a goal and assist in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Ipswich Town.

The 18-year-old was handed his first Premier League start against the Tractor Boys in place of the injured Mathys Tel, having shown glimpses of his potential off the bench against Leeds United and Crystal Palace.

With 15 minutes gone at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Williams-Barnett muscled his way beyond Abdoul Ouattara to meet Pedro Porro's cross and bundle the ball into the back of the net for the opening goal.

The 2008-born youngster followed up his maiden Premier League goal with a fine assist in the second period, driving down the left-hand side and crossing for Dominic Solanke to crash home.

Williams-Barnett made way for Savio in the 64th minute, having been booked shortly after Solanke's goal, but not without becoming Tottenham's third-youngest Premier League scorer ever.

At 18 years, one month and 20 days old, Williams-Barnett is only older than Andy Turner and Gareth Bale when they scored their first Premier League goals for Tottenham.

Turner holds the club record, having scored at just 17 years and five months against Everton in 1992, while Bale was just four days younger than Williams-Barnett is now when he netted against Fulham in September 2007.

Furthermore, Williams-Barnett has overtaken Tottenham traitor Sol Campbell on the list, as the latter was 18 years and two months old when he scored his maiden Spurs Premier League goal.

Aaron Lennon, Reto Ziegler and Dele Alli are the only other players in the top 10 to have scored their first Tottenham Premier League goals in the 2000s.

While Williams-Barnett stole the spotlight at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the teenager did not quite manage to break either a club or Premier League record.

Despite both scoring and setting up a goal in North London, Williams-Barnett is only the second-youngest player to both score and assist in a Premier League game, behind Michael Owen.

The former Ballon d'Or winner was just 17 years and 364 days old when he scored and assisted for Liverpool against Crystal Palace in 1997, before also doing so against Leeds United at 18 years and 12 days.

Nevertheless, Williams-Barnett has made his case to also start next Sunday's clash away to Sunderland, as well as the first North London derby of the season on December 6.

Spurs' victory over Ipswich has lifted De Zerbi's side up to ninth in the Premier League table on 15 points from 11 matches, just three points worse off than fourth-placed Bournemouth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026.

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

In a recent development, 'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'.

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness.

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list.

Industry observers note that joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an key part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences.

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Recent findings suggest that called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

According to recent reports, there were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010).

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Sources indicate that storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

St Louis City vs Los Angeles FC - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 21 Nov 2026 18:37.
  • In search of their first MLS playoff victory, St Louis City will welcome Los Angeles FC to Energizer Park for game one of that best-of-three series on Monday.
  • A 1-0 win at the Houston Dynamo ensured St Louis finished third in the Western Conference MLS standings while Los Angeles wound up in sixth, losing 2-1 to the Seattle Sounders on Decision Day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 21 Nov 2026 18:37.

In search of their first MLS playoff victory, St Louis City will welcome Los Angeles FC to Energizer Park for game one of that best-of-three series on Monday.

A 1-0 win at the Houston Dynamo ensured St Louis finished third in the Western Conference MLS standings while Los Angeles wound up in sixth, losing 2-1 to the Seattle Sounders on Decision Day.

For the first time since their inaugural campaign in 2023, St Louis have made the post-season, finishing with 54 points in 2026.

Under Yoann Demet, this team earned 22 more points this year when compared to 2025 and were just two points short of equaling their best-ever campaign in 2023.

While they won nine regular-season affairs at Energizer Park this year, on Monday this team will try to snap a three-match MLS winless run at home, collecting just one point over that stretch.

St Louis have lost their only two playoff outings and have not been in front for a single second in any of those post-season fixtures.

During the regular season, they failed to lose a single league game at home when netting the opening goal, dropping points in only two of those instances.

In 2026, they had a perfect home record against the two LA clubs in MLS, holding on to a narrow 2-1 home win over LAFC in May.

Los Angeles FC were not satisfied with the direction they were heading in this fall, but their coaching change has made little difference.

Since Xavi Tamarit took over from Marc Dos Santos, the Black and Gold have claimed only one victory in league play and will try to avoid losing three straight matches to MLS teams on Monday for the second time this year.

Tamarit is still seeking his first domestic away triumph as the interim manager, while LAFC have not won an MLS away game since July against the Los Angeles Galaxy (3-0).

While they struggled on the road this season, the 2022 league champions have not lost in 90 minutes in their last two playoff outings as the visitors.

During the regular season, they conceded the second-fewest goals in the Western Conference (40) while averaging the third-fewest goals allowed per match in MLS (1.2).

The Black and Gold have earned points in seven of their eight all-time league meetings with St Louis City, including two wins and three clean sheets overall at Energizer Park.

St Louis City Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis City form (all competitions):.

Los Angeles FC Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis midfielder Carlo Holse is doubtful for game one due to a knee injury, Celio Pompeu is still recovering from a cruciate ligament tear, while Roman Burki will hope to return from concussion protocol.

Lukas MacNaughton had the only goal in their victory versus the Dynamo, and Ben Lundt made six stops to collect the clean sheet in place of Burki.

As for LAFC, Jacob Shaffelburg is unlikely to feature because of a rib fracture, Hugo Lloris is recovering from a rib injury of his own, Aaron Long has a head injury and Timothy Tillman is questionable due to a pelvic issue.

Son Heung-min has scored in his last three playoff games, while Eddie Segura had the only goal in their Decision Day defeat against Seattle.

St Louis City possible starting lineup:.

Burki; MacNaughton, Baumgartl, Fall; Wallem, Polvara, Durkin, Totland; Downs, Navarro, Ostrak.

Los Angeles FC possible starting lineup:.

Carter; Hollingshead, Porteous, Segura, Cheberko; Choiniere, Delgado; Sieb, Walta, Bouanga; Heung-min.

Neither side were all that convincing down the stretch of the regular season, but the visitors have some proven performers who have stepped it up in knockout matches, and we believe that experience will give LAFC a narrow win in game one.

Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest: Marco Rose hails 'quite impressive' Evanilson after Cherries set latest club record

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (378 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 18:44.
  • Bournemouth set a upcoming club record by claiming a 2-0 victory over Nottingham Forest on Saturday afternoon.
  • After carrying an eight-game winning run into the international break, Bournemouth returned to action with another successful outing in their home meeting with Oliver Glasner's side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 18:44.

Bournemouth set a upcoming club record by claiming a 2-0 victory over Nottingham Forest on Saturday afternoon.

After carrying an eight-game winning run into the international break, Bournemouth returned to action with another successful outing in their home meeting with Oliver Glasner's side.

Evanilson opened the scoring just shy of the 20-minute mark, before Justin Kluivert scored what proved to be the game's final goal in first-half stoppage time.

As a result, Bournemouth have now won nine consecutive games in all competitions for the first time in their history.

They have claimed five of those victories in the Premier League, two in the Europa League and one in the EFL Cup.

Their current run of form has surpassed two separate eight-game winning streaks they enjoyed in 1998-99 and 2012-13.

What makes Bournemouth's run all the more impressive is the fact they have recorded seven clean sheets in their last nine games, representing a remarkable improvement from the side that shipped five goals against Chelsea on October 10.

When asked about Bournemouth's historic run, Rose told BBC Match of the Day: "We are not looking for records, we are just looking for the next game and talking about the next game.

According to recent reports, "We took the right approach. We were ready for this game, We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did, especially in the first half, really well.

"That is why it was a top performance and a deserved win.".

First six PL games this season: LDDDLL Next five PL games: WWWWW Marco Rose is cooking. ?‍?

Evanilson has netted seven goals in Bournemouth's winning run, including one in each of his last five competitive appearances.

In fact, the Brazilian has scored in six successive top-flight matches, making it the longest scoring streak in Bournemouth's Premier League history.

Praising his star striker, Rose remarked: "The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep. The way he scores is quite impressive.".

After climbing up to fourth spot in the Premier League table, Bournemouth will now turn their focus towards Thursday's Europa League away clash against Celta Vigo.

  • Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a fresh £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.
  • I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular fresh 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a fresh £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.

I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular fresh 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.

Interestingly, the meeting came in a week when Jacobo Solis, the influential Public Investment Fund executive and club director who is rarely seen in the city, was also present. The Spaniard’s involvement is viewed as extremely significant by those close to the project, and we understand an announcement on the club’s stadium looks is now ‘very close’.

The high-level meeting with Goldman Sachs is a major indication the club's board will recommend the development of a fresh stadium rather than redeveloping St James’, and I understand the former is currently the preference.

According to recent reports, there has been significant outlay on various surveys around Leazes Park in recent months. I reported in April how the presence of bats in the area was one environmental complication they had to overcome. The club has since undertaken extensive work around animal and plant life.

The alternative remains a St James’ expansion, taking the capacity to 60,000, but chief executive David Hopkinson and others among the top brass are well aware that only a fresh, multi-purpose home would allow Newcastle to compete financially with the world’s biggest clubs.

A secret meeting with representatives from Goldman Sachs is the strongest indication yet the club are preparing to leave St James' Park rather than redevelop it.

According to recent reports, in April, Daily Mail Sport revealed an architect’s drawing of how the latest, three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated.

Plans of the upcoming stadium reveal an exterior that has been likened to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena.

The proposed funding model combines borrowing, owner investment and potentially outside investors, with the debt sitting with Newcastle rather than the ownership. That makes the involvement of Goldman Sachs particularly significant as the club look to turn their ambitious aims into a financially viable reality.

According to recent reports, sources have described the circular design of a newly introduced stadium, and in April we revealed an architect’s drawing of how the three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated, but the exterior has been likened to both Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena and Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium by those who have seen images and video.

Club sources say they are continuing to work on options and plans for a new stadium. But the visit of Goldman Sachs – and the simultaneous presence of one of PIF's most influential figures – suggests that work behind the scenes is moving towards a decisive stage.

Having covered this story for several years, I now believe PIF will be asked to sign off on a fresh stadium development ahead of an announcement in early 2027.

Dedic case closed - but he's told to bow out.

Amar Dedic has been given a rap on the knuckles and handed over his bow and arrows after the Newcastle defender’s ‘suspicious activity’ triggered a major police operation earlier this month.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed on November 5 that the Bosnian was at the centre of a search involving at least six patrol cars after he was spotted carrying the hunting weaponry at a Northumberland beauty spot.

A concerned 999 caller, believing there could be a threat to the public, reported seeing him and a friend walking with the equipment near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the Harlow Hill area, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were intercepted in a blaze of blue lights around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Newcastle United's Amar Dedic has had his bow and arrows taken away from him after causing a major incident earlier this month.

Sources indicate that in a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic and his friend. After lengthy discussions at the roadside, police were satisfied that Dedic was using the weaponry for recreational use, but their investigation remained open.

Recent findings suggest that however, I can confirm the matter is now closed and the 24-year-old has been reminded of UK law by police and the club. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in this country.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson told me: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, November 4, we received a report of suspicious activity in the Harlow Hill area.

‘It was reported that two men had been witnessed in possession of bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road. Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

'At that time, it was understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Following a number of enquiries, this has now been confirmed. The two men have since forfeited the bow and arrows and words of advice have been given to the pair. The case has now been closed.’.

Dedic took the confusion in good spirit, posting a picture of Lord of the Rings character Legolas, known for his prowess with a bow and arrow, on his social media page.

Joelinton has not yet been ruled out of the Tyne-Wear derby, despite fears over a significant injury lay-off.

I revealed on November 4 that the Brazilian had suffered a fresh muscle strain and this was confirmed by Matthias Jaissle the following day. There has been a suggestion this week that the period out could extend towards Christmas, but sources have played down that possibility.

Sources indicate that I understand Joelinton is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures. This could still be too soon for the visit of Sunderland on December 6, but the noises around the midfielder have definitely been more optimistic in the past 24 hours. The 30-year-old is expected to be the only senior absentee from the squad that takes on Arsenal this weekend.

Joelinton (left) is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures.

According to recent reports, newcastle will NOT be signing Gambian triallists Omar Marong and Alieu Saine. I understand that, while the 16-year-olds have impressed during a two-week stay, club chiefs have decided that those already on the books are of greater potential.

Marong and Saine played in a 6-0 win over the i2i International Soccer Academy on Friday, and winger Saine chipped in with two assists. However, while there is a feeling both will secure moves to Europe in due course, Newcastle will keep a watching brief for now.

It has been revealed that the pair are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and were identified by the club’s fresh global talent team. They caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals.

According to recent reports, neither player could have signed permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle were keen to assess their potential. It is likely that players of a similar profile from Africa will arrive on trial in the future.

Arteta to meet old foe at St James'.

It has been revealed that both Jaissle and Mikel Arteta will walk suspension tightropes at St James’ Park on Saturday. The Newcastle and Arsenal bosses are on two bookings for the season – and a third means a one-game touchline ban.

Interestingly, the fourth official with whom Arteta clashed at Sunderland earlier this season will be on duty. Elliot Bell repeatedly warned Arteta not to step from his technical zone at the Stadium of Light.

Industry observers note that when the Spaniard infringed on Sunderland’s managerial area for a third time, referee John Brooks issued a yellow card. Arteta then appeared to sarcastically target Bell with a ‘just tick the box’ gesture.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is a booking away from a one-game touchline ban.

The 2023 match between Newcastle and Arsenal at St James' Park was settled by a controversial winner, with Joelinton accused of a push on Gabriel.

Industry observers note that in another twist, Stuart Attwell will be the VAR this weekend. He was the referee in charge when Newcastle beat Arsenal 1-0 three years ago. The controversial winning goal that night was scored by Anthony Gordon amid suspicion the ball had run out of play before Joe Willock crossed.

Joelinton was then accused by Arsenal of a push on defender Gabriel, while Gordon looked offside. All three incidents survived VAR checks and Attwell’s on-field decision stood.

Industry observers note that arteta was furious and branded the decision an ‘absolute disgrace’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arsenal subsequently issued an official statement backing his criticism and demanded improved refereeing standards. Arteta was charged by the FA over his comments but was eventually cleared.

However, the Premier League's independent Key Match Incidents panel ruled by a 4-1 majority that the goal had correctly been allowed to stand.

Finally, after James Trafford starred during England's 3-2 win in Spain this week, a brilliant match I was lucky enough to cover, one reader reached out to ask about an XI of players Newcastle have missed out on.

The club tried to sign Trafford on three occasions under Eddie Howe, and even as recently as this summer he appeared destined for Tyneside.

So, with thanks to the idea from Ian Spencer, here is the ‘what might have been’ XI of Newcastle targets who came close to signing….

Newcastle's What Might Have Been XI (3-5-2): James Trafford; Abdukodir Khusanov, Tosin Adarabioyo, Marc Guehi; Ivan Fresneda, Johan Manzambi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, James Maddison, Victor Munoz; Joao Pedro, Hugo Ekitike.

It has been revealed that would this XI beat the current side? Answers in the comments below please!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 19:30, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 20:07.
  • Arsenal spurned the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League table as they were forced to come from behind to draw 2-2 with Newcastle United at St James' Park.
  • Warned to expect a "hellish" fixture at a ground where they have not had much luck in recent years, the champions were in the ascendancy from the off and deservedly went into half time ahead courtesy of Eberechi Eze's first-time finish.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 19:30, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 20:07.

Arsenal spurned the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League table as they were forced to come from behind to draw 2-2 with Newcastle United at St James' Park.

Warned to expect a "hellish" fixture at a ground where they have not had much luck in recent years, the champions were in the ascendancy from the off and deservedly went into half time ahead courtesy of Eberechi Eze's first-time finish.

Matthias Jaissle's men were booed off at half time after generating just 0.08 Expected Goals during the opening period, but that number shot up just four minutes into the second half, when a gift from Martin Odegaard handed Harvey Barnes an equaliser against the run of play.

Barnes's strike triggered a magnificent Newcastle response, one that saw them rewarded with the game's third goal through Malick Thiaw just past the hour mark following a corner scramble.

However, the momentum pendulum swung back Arsenal's way shortly after, as the effervescent Noni Madueke drew the holders level to set up a grand-stand finish.

Nine minutes of added time was not enough for either team to snatch a winner, as Arsenal extended their lead over Manchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion to six points, while Newcastle remain 12th with 13 points.

For all of Arsenal's first-half dominance, the Gunners were guilty of a perpetual shortcoming in the Arteta era; not putting the game to bed before the break.

Staunch Newcastle defending and shoddy Arsenal finishing denied the visitors a healthier first-half advantage, and while the champions cut complacent figures at the start of the second half, Jaissle's half-time team talk worked a treat.

Odegaard's blunder helped the hosts on their way, and Arsenal found themselves unfamiliarly rattled for a good 30 minutes, until the increasingly impressive Madueke came to the fore again.

However, the winger himself admitted that his side should have been at least three to the good at half time, yet more evidence that a killer finisher is a matter of priority for the January transfer window.

"Absolutely clinical!" Eberechi Eze scores his first Premier League goal of the season to give Arsenal the lead ? https://t.co/34IbZuuJuN.

Seven months after his last Premier League goal - against the Magpies - the Englishman does it again, rifling in a slick side-footed strike from 12 yards after Kai Havertz's delightful through ball.

Havertz had robbed Lewis Hall of possession before slipping in Eze, who left Lukas Hornicek rooted to the spot.

"Horrendous error!" Harvey Barnes puts Newcastle level ? https://t.co/YWrHZPxBIo.

A howler from Odegaard, a flicker of hope for Newcastle!

The Arsenal captain tries to volley a throw-in close to his own penalty area, but gets his connection all wrong and slices the ball into William Osula's path.

The Newcastle striker spots Barnes in acres of space in the left of the box, and the latter takes one touch to set himself before calmly slotting home into the bottom corner!

Malick Thiaw is in the right place to fire it in and give Newcastle the lead against Arsenal! ? https://t.co/nthaH3aOJD.

When we talk about a game of two halves, this is exactly what we mean.

Dan Burn finds himself all alone as a corner is floated in; replays show that Jurrien Timber - his marker - was being held back by Osula as he tried to catch up to him.

The towering Newcastle defender heads the ball back into the danger area, and after an almighty scramble, Thiaw pokes home from a yard out!

Noni Madueke equalises for Arsenal! ? https://t.co/VNXOoNDxiJ.

Champions respond how champions respond.

Odegaard just broke down a counter-attack by picking the wrong pass, but the Arsenal captain gets it right this time, laying off Madueke on the right-hand side.

The winger cuts inside, works a yard for a shot from inside the D, and the ball finds its way into the bottom corner via Hornicek's gloves.

The Newcastle goalkeeper ought to have done better, but credit the free-flowing move from the visitors, who are level again!

"I reckon 2-2 was a fair result." Noni Madueke reflects on Arsenal's performance against Newcastle at St James' Park ? https://t.co/UfDi5SGgat.

Both frustrating and fascinating to watch for Arsenal fans, Madueke once again proved a capable deputy for Bukayo Saka on the right.

The England international had six shots in total, made one key pass and registered four successful dribbles, albeit while missing two major chances that could, or should, have been the difference between Arsenal taking home either one or three points.

Possession: Newcastle 34%-66% Arsenal.

Shots on target: Newcastle 3-4 Arsenal.

Harvey Barnes for Newcastle: 50 G/A 35 goals 15 assists https://t.co/3TMxbJSB7i.

Arsenal resume their Champions League campaign at home to Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday evening, before the major one against Manchester City in next Sunday's Premier League showdown.

Meanwhile, Newcastle have over a week to recuperate before they travel to Arsenal's closest Premier League title challengers Brighton & Hove Albion next Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” noted Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sources indicate that sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”.

Sources indicate that the veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”.

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

According to recent reports, palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Recent findings suggest that bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

The veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

It has been revealed that angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

According to recent reports, suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.
  • Industry observers note that one source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

Industry observers note that one source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are noted to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Industry observers note that van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which highlights his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their fresh deals.

Alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing issue for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

Recent findings suggest that it was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

Slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

He is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

The Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Sources indicate that regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

Confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

In the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

In the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

In a recent development, since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Substantial Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a new-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Liverpool need to see more from their substantial-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton boxer Harlem Eubank expects another "special event" as he returns to the Brighton Centre on February 5.

Eubank, 32, will be up against significant-punching American Greg Outlaw in a 12-round welterweight contest, which will also be screened live on DAZN.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

A win against Outlaw - who is ranked No 13 by the WBA - could tee-up some lucrative fights in 2027 against the likes of American boxers Devin Haney, Teofimo Lopez, Ryan Garcia and Britain's Conor Benn.

Eubank lost on points last time out against Frenchman David Papot in an entertaining clash at the Cooper Box last July but remains unbeaten in his three previous fights at the Brighton Centre.

Timo Schwarzkopf, Tyrone McKenna and Josh Wagner have all been beaten by Eubank at the Brighton Centre and the lifelong Brighton and Hove Albion fan expects to make the Outlaw his fourth victim on the south coast.

Sources indicate that "I'm excited for this one," said Eubank to Sussex World. "Returning to the Brighton Centre, I love fighting there.

Recent findings suggest that "It's really become my home venue and there's a great energy there. People love coming out to witness a show, and that's what we're ready for on 5 February.

"The Outlaw has a solid record. He's top 15 in the WBA, top 20 in the IBF. A highly ranked guy. I expect him to come and really fight. I'm expecting a good test, and I'm excited to challenge myself once again.".

Eubank will have his hands full with the Outlaw on February 5 but the Brighton boxer - who is the nephew of former two-weight world champion Chris Eubank Sr - can‘t resist looking ahead to some big fights.

Sources indicate that “Devin Haney, Teofimo Lopez, Ryan Garcia,” stated Eubank to Sussex World. “I like them fights, the American guys that have a bit of flair to them.

“I feel like I've got my own style and own flair, and I always think when a Brit goes up against top American fighters, you really engage the British boxing public.

“I'd love to represent Great Britain against one of the top Americans.”.

Industry observers note that he also wants to renew the Eubank-Benn rivalry and believes a fight with Conor Benn is always an option and a “comfortable” night’s work. Eubank Snr had two epic battles with Nigel Benn in the 1990s and Conor Benn (Nigel’s son) has also had two fights with Chris Eubank Jnr (Harlem’s first-cousin).

Conor Benn is currently plotting his route back into top level boxing after he was blasted in less than two rounds by Garcia last September.

Eubank remarked: “Yes, definitely. I would love that fight. If he rebuilds, he obviously just got taken out at world level.

“But I think that fight will always be there. It's a fight that I've wanted for a number of years. It's a comfortable fight.

Industry observers note that “I've fought many better guys in my previous fights. It's a fight that can happen anytime really.”.

Another Eubank v Benn is a very sellable fight for the future but Eubank is also working his way back from his loss to Papot. It was a fast-paced and entertaining bout that saw Eubank down twice and Papot once.

The Brighton boxer displayed tremendous courage against the accomplished Frenchman in an topsy-turvy and bloody battle for both men.

Sources indicate that “It was a very entertaining night,” Eubank remarked to Sussex World. “ Very closely contested fight against a great fighter.

“I feel like it was a fight that revealed a lot of different parts of my game, not just skill set, but mentally, physically.

“All the components that you can't teach. All the components that I know I have in my game, but it takes certain experiences for you to show the public.

According to recent reports, “So I can take a lot away from it. I feel like I was just scratching the surface in terms of how good I can be.

“Maybe it [the loss] was required for me to introduce that side of me and show people different parts of my game.”.

Tickets for Eubank vs Outlaw at the Brighton Centre on February 5, go on sale on Monday, November 23 at 10am.

#72164. Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 44m • 📚 Deep Dive (8857 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 44 min read (8857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~44 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4.
  • Recent findings suggest that unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4.
  • The particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7,8,9,10,11,12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

Recent findings suggest that unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4. Depending on the relative weight of those energy terms, many different phenomena have been observed: the Hofstadter butterfly depending mainly on the van der Waals coupling13,14,15, commensurate–incommensurate phase transitions driven by van der Waals–strain competition5,6 and flat-band formation that probably involves all three contributions and facilitates superconductivity and correlated insulating phase 16,17,18.

The particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies. Varying their relative contributions can switch the system between different atomic arrangements, resulting in structural phase transitions potentially accompanied by the emergence of fresh electronic phases. This points to a rich underlying phase diagram. Yet experimental platforms that allow controlled exploration of this phase space so far have been lacking.

Industry observers note that here we demonstrate that, by careful tuning of the balance between these competing interactions in a three-layer van der Waals heterostructure, we can reach simultaneous structural and electronic phase transitions, controlled through layer charging, magnetic field or temperature variation. We engineer these transitions in a heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hBN and mhBN on either side: mhBN/graphene/hBN. In such heterostructures, strain is greatly enhanced because mhBN, unlike its bulk counterpart, is free to contract and corrugate (the strain amplitude is controlled by the number of hBN layers), leading to strongly enhanced surface reconstruction19,20,21. The van der Waals interaction of this system is likewise enhanced by the double alignment and can be tuned by gate-charging the graphene layer.

Sources indicate that in such heterostructure devices, the structural phase transition reveals itself through an abrupt, global and reversible switch of the stacking configuration, which entails a change of symmetry (analogous to the Bernal-to-rhombohedral transition in graphite22,23,24,25) and results in distinct reconstruction modes observed directly by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). It is accompanied by a unique electronic phase transition: switching between p-doping and n-doping of graphene. Unlike conventional doping, the doping levels before and after the phase transition are discrete rather than continuous in nature, always taking an integer or ‘quantized’ value corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons per moiré unit cell, which we hereafter term integer doping. We attribute this integer doping to electrons (holes) being trapped in the strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (PLLs), formed by the strong moiré surface reconstruction; these localized states constitute flat bands in k-space, as predicted theoretically7,8,9,10,11 and confirmed by STM measurements12. The structural transition alters the atomic arrangement, modifying both the strain and scalar-potential landscapes. In reciprocal space, we interpret this as switching the hybridization of these flat bands between the valence band (AB phase) and the conduction band (AA phase), inverting the sign of the integer doping.

Sources indicate that our heterostructure consists of monolayer graphene that is double-aligned, on one side to hBN and on the other side to mhBN (refs. 19,20). Unlike single alignment, such double-aligned ‘sandwich’ heterostructures can exhibit either parallel or antiparallel orientations corresponding to the 0° and 180° angle alignment between the top and bottom hBN (refs. 2,19,26). The results obtained on both types of device are similar, so in the main text, we focus on the parallel orientation, presenting the analysis for the antiparallel orientation in Supplementary Information Sections 20, 23, 26 and 28 (Supplementary Figs. 30, 41 and 42).

For either orientation, two energetically competing stacking configurations exist (Fig. 1c,d), which are interconvertible by sliding the mhBN by one interatomic distance relative to the bulk hBN (detailed explanation and simple schematics in Supplementary Information Section 21; Supplementary Figs. 31 and 32). This is analogous to the transition between ABC (rhombohedral) and ABA (Bernal) trilayer graphene, in which a small shift of one of the layers leads to strong reconfigurations of the electronic bands22,23,24,25.

External parameters (such as carrier density n, magnetic field B and temperature T) define one coordinate axis, whereas the intrinsic stacking order of the sandwich heterostructure defines the other. Two local energy minima exist corresponding to AA and AB stacking configurations, with their dominant stackings shown in c and d, respectively. Blue and red arrows indicate transitions between these configurations; solid arrows denote states realized under continuous tuning of external parameters, whereas dashed arrows mark the abrupt structural phase transition, matching the solid and dashed lines in the experiments shown in Fig. 3a–c. b, Moiré-induced corrugation observed in a double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN device, measured at room temperature by AFM. Inset shows the corrugation profile along the light blue line. Phonon squeezing reduces corrugation at low temperatures. The unit cell outlined in black matches that in g. c,d, Schematic illustrations of the competing sandwich configurations at double-aligned interfaces: AB (c) and AA (d) stacking configurations. e–h, MD simulations of strain distributions. Panels g and h show our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN configurations with AB and AA stacking configurations, respectively, and panels e and f show reference calculations for double-aligned hBN/graphene/hBN configurations. Comparison highlights the notable role of mhBN on strain enhancement, leading to much stronger reconstruction patterns—triangular and hexagonal reconstructions, respectively. Dashed circles indicate vertices of domains arising from these two reconstruction types, on which strain-induced PLLs develop, as shown on the right. The yellow-to-orange gradient bar indicates increasing strain amplitude. i, The theoretical calculated corrugation of the graphene–hBN interface as a function of the twist angle.

Unlike previous studies that apply a mechanical tool such as an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope tip to locally ‘iron’ the sample to toggle the stacking configurations in confined regions of sample27,28, our system allows global, reversible switching between the two stacking states simply by tuning external parameters, including carrier density n, magnetic field B or temperature T. Such all-electronic control is far better suited to device integration and to triggering latest phenomena in transport measurements. The schematic in Fig. 1a illustrates the full phase diagram defined by these external parameters and the intrinsic stacking order, in which the two local minima correspond to the competing AB and AA stacking configurations. Accompanying this switch, the moiré-induced strain distribution and thus the lattice reconstruction changes from triangular to hexagonal patterns (Fig. 1e–h; see also the STM images in Fig. 5a,b), ultimately leading to different pseudomagnetic field (PMF) distributions2,29 (Fig. 5e,f) and different band reconfigurations (Fig. 5g–j).

We emphasize that the mhBN is essential for enhancing such lattice reconstruction of graphene, as mhBN itself can accommodate a finite amount of strain, allowing both layers (mhBN and graphene) to undergo very strong relaxation. The molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, comparing mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1g,h) and hBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1e,f) heterostructures, clearly demonstrate that the presence of mhBN greatly amplifies the periodic strain induced by moiré reconstruction. The experimental evidence, including room-temperature atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurement of the corrugation (Fig. 1b) and the same measurement with varying hBN layer numbers (1–4 layers; Supplementary Information Section 13; Supplementary Fig. 19) and their corresponding transport properties, is presented in Supplementary Information Section 4. As well as mhBN, alignment also markedly influences the strain, as shown by the calculated corrugation with respect to the twist angle in Fig. 1i.

Two types of transport device are discussed in the main text: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN (Fig. 2a) and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 2b). In the former, the mhBN–hBN interface is intentionally misaligned by 15° to achieve superlubricity, preserving the double-aligned sandwich structure. The two architectures are complementary: the dual-gated capped devices enable higher carrier concentrations and allow the roles of doping and the displacement field to be disentangled (Supplementary Information Section 8), whereas the non-capped mhBN/graphene/hBN structure develops stronger reconstruction, in particular the out-of-plane corrugation at the graphene–mhBN interface (Supplementary Information Section 30).

Sources indicate that for both architectures, double alignment of graphene to the hBN crystals on both sides was confirmed by AFM, Raman and transport measurements (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 2). We emphasize that both the double alignment and the presence of mhBN are crucial for the effects we observe, as corroborated by seven types of reference device, none of which exhibit the transition (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4; Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

Industry observers note that first, let us examine the initial-state transfer curves (blue) of the two device types in Fig. 2c,d. In the hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN sample, the neutrality point of graphene remains at zero doping, whereas the mhBN/graphene/hBN structure exhibits p-doping. Notably, this p-doping level closely approximates 2n0 (n0 corresponds to doping of one charge carrier per moiré plaquette). In 8 of 9 unencapsulated mhBN/graphene/hBN devices (blue dots in Fig. 2f), the p-doping is quantized at Nn0 (N is an integer between 1 and 4), growing with the moiré period but always fixed at integer multiples of n0.

In a recent development, in Fig. 2e,f, the moiré period, determined from the carrier density of secondary Dirac points, exceeds in many samples the rigid-lattice limit of 14 nm (set by the 1.8% graphene–hBN lattice mismatch) and even reaches 17.7 nm, a consequence of the strain enhancement by mhBN and double alignment19,20 (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4).

Industry observers note that by applying a large positive gate voltage above a certain threshold, a phase transition can be initiated: the moiré period remains unchanged but the samples become n-doped, again by an integer number of electrons per moiré plaquette, for both bottom-gated and dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c,d), and consistently across samples with different moiré sizes (Fig. 2e,f; Supplementary Information Section 3; Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). Comprehensive control experiments (Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14; Supplementary Figs. 9–11 and 20–22) verify that this transition and the integer doping are intrinsic, excluding artefacts such as contamination. We emphasize that the integer doping is a direct observation requiring no fitting or registration procedure. As is well established for graphene superlattices5,6,7, the neutrality point–secondary Dirac point separation is fixed at four electrons per moiré unit cell. In Fig. 2c, the post-transition neutrality point (red) falls precisely at the midpoint between the pre-transition neutrality point and the secondary Dirac point (blue) and hence corresponds to exactly two electrons per moiré unit cell, as highlighted by the equally spaced ruler.

According to recent reports, note that for the dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c), the gate voltage was applied simultaneously through top and bottom gates along the D = 0 line30 (dashed line in Fig. 3a). The switching depends only on the total carrier concentration and not on the displacement field (Supplementary Information Section 8; Supplementary Fig. 14). This mechanism fundamentally differs from recently reported two-dimensional ferroelectric systems, in which transitions occur through external electric-field-induced polarization changes26,31,32.

Sources indicate that to investigate the transition dynamics and reproducibility, we conducted a series of Vtg–Vbg mappings and repeated switching tests (Rxx in Fig. 3; Rxy in Supplementary Fig. 24). Figure 3a–c reveals several Dirac points separated by intervals of four electrons per moiré plaquette5,6,7, marked with blue (before transition) or red (after transition) lines or arrows.

Recent findings suggest that the phase transition occurs at Vtg = +3.9 V, Vbg = +5.3 V corresponding to ntotal = 3.75 × 1012 cm−2 along the D = 0 line in Fig. 3a. Following the transition, all features shift by two electrons per moiré plaquette. This shift throughout the entire superlattice spectrum clearly indicates that the moiré period is unchanged. The recovery occurs at Vtg = −5.0 V, Vbg = −6.9 V (corresponding to −4.85 × 1012 cm−2), also along the D = 0 line, restoring the entire gate dependence (Fig. 3b). Comparing Fig. 3c with Fig. 3a demonstrates that different Vtg–Vbg ranges and sweep protocols do not affect the transition characteristics: it occurs at identical gate points, as a single discrete event at the critical voltage rather than a continuous evolution.

Figure 3d illustrates the transition dynamics through sequential measurements (swp1–swp8), with dashed lines at +5.3 V and −6.9 V marking the critical voltages for the forward and reverse transitions, respectively. Below the critical voltage, no transition occurs (swp1–swp2); on reaching it, the transition happens (swp3–swp4), at a critical voltage independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15; Supplementary Fig. 23). Similar behaviour is observed for the reverse transition (steps swp4–swp7). Figure 3f,g indicates zoomed-in views around the critical voltages for both the forward and reverse transitions. At the moment of transition, the resistance jumps from one state to another without any intermediate states, consistent with the abrupt translation of features observed in Vtg–Vbg mappings of Fig. 3a–c. Once the transition is induced, further increasing the gate voltage yields no continuous effect, indicating a saturation mechanism defined by the moiré unit cell capacity rather than the strength of the applied field. This behaviour differs markedly from that of ferroelectrics, for which polarization scales continuously with the applied field. The switching is fully reproducible: 100 consecutive cycles yield curves that overlap precisely (Fig. 3d, top). All behaviours discussed above support that the observed phase transition is a first-order-like transition (further information in Supplementary Information Section 43).

Notably, the transition can also be controlled by the magnetic field. Mapping the transition from 13 T down to 0 T (Fig. 3e) highlights that the transition is suppressed at high field, even for gate voltages far exceeding the critical value, and reappears at exactly the same critical voltage once the field drops below Bcrit = 3.8 T. The origin of this suppression remains to be established; we note, however, that the magnetic length at critical field \(\sqrt{\hbar /e{B}_{{\rm{crit}}}}\approx 13.4\,{\rm{nm}}\) is comparable with the moiré period for this sample of 13.8 nm.

According to recent reports, in Fig. 3h, correlating Rxx with Rxy gives further information for theoretical analysis: the Hall-resistivity zero crossing (zero free carrier density nfree) occurs at a gate-induced density of two holes per moiré unit cell, the difference being compensated by localized electrons nloc.

To identify the origin of the phase transition, we consider the balance between elastic (strain) and van der Waals forces5,6, which can be modified through Coulomb interactions introduced by gate charging the graphene layer.

Using high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), we calculated the adhesion-energy distribution across the non-relaxed moiré plaquette, assuming perfect alignment of hBN on both sides, for the AB (Fig. 4a) and AA (Fig. 4b) relative configurations of the two hBN crystals (Supplementary Information Section 22; Supplementary Figs. 33–35). The relative energy of the two configurations can be compared by averaging the van der Waals potential over the entire moiré unit cell, as illustrated in Fig. 4c. The AB structure exhibits lower energy under neutral charging conditions (Fig. 4c–e). However, by assigning a negative charge on graphene above a certain threshold (corresponding to positive gate voltage applied) the AA configuration becomes more energetically favourable than AB (Fig. 4c,f,g), resulting in a structural phase transition from AB to AA.

a,b, Schematics of the two configurations (AB (a) and AA (b)) and three high-symmetry stacking sites for both configurations. The red arrows on the left side indicate a shift of one of the hBN layers by one interatomic distance. c, Schematic diagram of the relative stability (in terms of the average adhesion energy taken over the entire moiré plaquette) of the two configurations as a function of doping. The solid lines represent the energy-favourable state. The crossing of the blue and red lines indicates the occurrence of the transition. Electron doping (positive gate) switches the relative stability between the two configurations and the consequent modification of the interlayer adhesion is proposed to be the driving force. d–g, Distribution of the interlayer adhesion energy (Eadh) across the moiré plaquette for the AB (d,f) and AA (e,g) configurations in the case of zero (d,e) and n-type (f,g) external doping (induced by gating in our experiments). The graphs in the middle give the corresponding adhesion energies of the three high-symmetry stackings as a function of interlayer distance between graphene and the top and bottom boron nitride layers near the equilibrium spacing (2.7–4.0 Å).

Industry observers note that the energy evolution with doping arises from gate-introduced Coulomb interactions, which enter the competition between van der Waals forces and elastic energies5,6. The balance among these three factors can be understood by comparing the relative stability of the AB and AA stacking configurations at high-symmetry points (Fig. 4a,b), which are the most representative sites and capture the qualitative trends under gating. Specifically, n-type doping substantially reduces the interlayer potential of AA-3 stacking: there, carbon atoms are vertically aligned with boron and the added electrons on carbon are strongly attracted to the positive charge on boron arising from the ionic nature of B–N bonds33. By contrast, the interlayer potential of AA-2 stacking is slightly elevated by the repulsion between the added electrons and the negatively charged nitrogen, whereas AA-1 and all three high-symmetry sites of the AB alignment remain almost unchanged, as the interaction of added electrons with boron is compensated by their interaction with nitrogen. This picture is substantiated by DFT calculations (Fig. 4d–g; Supplementary Information Sections 22–27). We can generalize the similar gate-induced phase transitions to other systems in which at least one of the multiply aligned layers has electropolarity (Supplementary Information Section 37).

We now turn to the origin of the integer doping in graphene, which we attribute to strain-induced PLLs localized at the vertices of the reconstructed moiré domains. The reconstructed phases for AB and AA configurations are directly visualized through STM measurements (STM images of different regions, and of a reference single-aligned graphene/hBN region on the same flake, are shown in Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13) and theoretically simulated by MD calculations (Fig. 5a,b). On the basis of the atomic displacements calculated by MD, we obtained the strain distribution in the reconstructed moiré unit cell (schematics shown in Fig. 5c,d), as well as the associated pseudomagnetic field7,8,9,10,11,34 (left panels of Fig. 5e,f) (Supplementary Information Sections 24, 29 and 31).

The reconstruction results in distinct strain fields for the AB and AA configurations (Fig. 5c,d). For the AB configuration, it is the AB-1 and AB-3 stackings that have much lower energy than AB-2 (Fig. 4d,f), so the reconstruction forms triangular domains of AB-1 and AB-3 stackings, accompanied by notable strain and out-of-plane corrugation at the AB-2 stacking (Fig. 5c). By contrast, for the AA configuration, it is the AA-3 stacking that has the lowest energy (Fig. 4e,g), leading to hexagonally reconstructed AA-3 moiré domain, with the strain concentrated at AA-2 and AA-1 stacked corners of the moiré plaquette (Fig. 5d). Here the predominance of in-plane strain in AA (versus out-of-plane corrugation in AB) originates from the mirror symmetry of the AA configuration, which yields negligible net out-of-plane force (Supplementary Information Section 38; Supplementary Fig. 54). In both cases, the strain results in strong PMF.
